items.label: text
items.text: There will be a stage at which [HIn(aq)] = [In-(aq)] and the indicator will appear orange. The exact pH at which this stage is reached can be determined using the equilibrium constant,Kin,for methyl orange.

items.label: formula
items.text: K_In = [H⁺(aq)][In⁻(aq)] / [HIn(aq)] = 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³

items.label: text
items.text: When [HIn(aq)] = [In-(aq)], the expression becomes: [H+(aq)] = 2.00 × 10-4 mol dm-3

items.label: text
items.text: This gives a pH of 3.70 for the 'half-way' stage. So, methyl orange will change colour at a pH of 3.70.

items.label: text
items.text: Notethat thispHvalueis alsothesameasthevalueofpK,for methylorange.Therefore,thepHatwhichdifferentindicatorswill change colour can be determined from their pKivalues.

items.label: section_header
items.text: pHRANGEOFINDICATORS

items.label: text
items.text: As a'rule of thumb',the red colour of methyl orange will first predominate when [HIn(aq)] is ten times [In-(aq)], and the yellow colour will predominate when [In-(aq)] is ten times [HIn(aq)].

items.label: text
items.text: The approximate pH at which each colour predominates can be calculated asfollows.

items.label: formula
items.text:
When [HIn(aq)] = 10[In⁻(aq)]:
[H⁺(aq)][In⁻(aq)] / 10[In⁻(aq)] = 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³

items.label: formula
items.text: [H⁺(aq)] = 2.00 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³

items.label: text
items.text: So, the pH at which the red colour first predominates is 2.70.

items.label: text
items.text: AsimilarcalculationwillshowthatthepHatwhichtheyellow colourfirstpredominates is 4.70.

items.label: text
items.text: The exact pH range of methyl orange is 3.10 to 4.40. This means that at pH values below 3.10, methyl orange will appear red. At pHvalues above4.40,methyl orangewill appearyellow.Between 3.10 and 4.40, methyl orange will be a shade of orange.

items.label: text
items.text: Table A shows the pKinvalues,pH ranges and colours of several common indicators.

items.label: table
items.text:
table A

| INDICATOR        |   pKin | pH RANGE   | COLOUR - HIn(aq)   | COLOUR - In-(aq)   |
|------------------|--------|------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| methyl orange    |   3.70 | 3.10-4.40  | red                | yellow             |
| bromophenol blue |   4.00 | 2.80-4.60  | yellow             | blue               |
| bromothymolblue  |   7.00 | 6.00-7.60  | yellow             | blue               |

items.label: section_header
items.text: CHOICEOFINDICATOR

items.label: text
items.text: A good indicator shows a complete colour change upon the addition of one drop of acid from the burette. This is necessary inordertoaccuratelydeterminetheendpointofthetitration.

items.label: text
items.text: Therefore,therehastobea minimumpH changeequivalent to the pH range of the indicator in order for the indicator to successfully determine the end point.

items.label: section_header
items.text: STRONGACID-STRONGBASETITRATION

items.label: text
items.text: Let us first of all consider the use of methyl orange and phenolphthalein as indicators for a strong acid-strong base titration.

items.label: text
items.text: Fig F shows the pH titration curve for 25 cm? of 1.00 mol dm-3 NaOH(aq) titrated with 1.00 mol dm-3 HCl(aq). The pH ranges of methylorangeandphenolphthaleinhavealsobeenincluded.

items.label: caption
items.text: figFStrong acid-strongbasepH curve.

items.label: text
items.text: You will notice that the pH range of each indicator falls within the steepsectionofthecurve,wherealargepHchangeisoccurring upontheadditionofjustonedropofacid.Thismeansthatboth indicators will change colour at the end point and therefore both aresuitable indicators touse in this titration.

items.label: section_header
items.text: WEAKACID-STRONGBASETITRATION

items.label: text
items.text: Wewill nowconsiderthesuitabilityofeachindicatorforaweak acid-strongbase titration.
